Container.Name: CineDock
Container.Overview: Rediscover your library. CineDock gives Plex, Emby or Jellyfin an enhanced browsing experience on the NVIDIA Shield TV, on an Amazon Fire TV Stick, on Zidoo media players, or in a browser on your computer or tablet.
Container.Changes:
### 4.8.6 (28 August 2026) - Televisions are told that TV app 0.2.7 exists. Televisions on 0.2.6 or older are now offered 0.2.7, which on boxes that hand playback to the device's own player - Zidoo players do this - is what makes the screen catch up when you come back from an episode; until now the one you had just finished was still offered as the next, and its tick did not appear until the app was restarted. 4.8.5 put the mechanism in place, 0.2.7 is the half that lives on the television, and this release is the only thing that tells anyone it is there. The television setup guide now also says to restart the box after installing the TV app, and why: installing an app leaves an Android television busy optimising code and reclaiming memory, and on boxes that hand playback to their own player that can end CineDock during the first thing you play - which looks exactly like a fault in the new version. A restart clears it. No other change to the container.
### 4.8.5 (28 August 2026) - A film no longer freezes part-way through. When a television's own player fills its buffer and then reads nothing for a quarter of an hour, the connection behind it can be dropped with part of the file still to come; CineDock had no answer to that, so the picture simply stopped and only skipping forward brought it back. It now re-opens the file at the exact byte it had reached and carries on, so the player never sees the join - reproduced and measured before release, with the connection killed eighteen minutes into a silence and 380 MB still owed, and every byte delivered intact. Also fixed: on Plex, a viewer signed in with a PIN saw a permanently empty More Like This on every title, and each visit to a series page silently began a whole-library scan that was thrown away when the page finished loading. Playback links now expire once unused - never while they are delivering a film - a media server's refusal is passed on as what it actually said rather than a generic failure, and its credentials are no longer sent on across a redirect to another machine, port or unencrypted connection. Televisions still on TV app 0.2.4 or 0.2.5 are now offered 0.2.6, the release that fixes the app closing at the end of an episode. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.6 (versionCode 8).
### 4.8.4 (27 August 2026) - A remote can mark one episode watched again. On a series page, Right on a highlighted episode steps onto the episode's own tick - the card stays lit beneath it - and OK marks that one episode watched or unwatched; Left steps back, and OK on the episode still plays it. The route had been missing since the one-page series redesign in 4.6.0 left only a keyboard's W key and a mouse click. The television Help and the cinedock.tv guide describe the new grammar, and televisions still on TV app 0.2.4 are now offered 0.2.5. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.5 (versionCode 7).
### 4.8.3 (27 August 2026) - Help worth the name. The television's Help now carries the full cinedock.tv guide, word for word - thirteen topics from the remote to Requests, with the guide's address and a QR code leading the page so help is point-your-phone-and-you-are-there. Pages that depend on something say so large: a TMDB key for biographies, Seerr for Requests, local trailer files for reliable television trailers. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.4 (versionCode 6).
### 4.8.2 (27 August 2026) - A faster series page, a Help worth the name, and CineDock stops curating. The curated shelves - Hidden Gems, Top by Actor or Director and Top from a Studio - are removed: your collections are yours to make, and CineDock does not curate for you. Recently Watched, Playlists and the Seasonal shelves stay. The television Help now walks every screen of the app, in the same order and words as the rewritten guide at cinedock.tv/guide. And opening a series from Continue Watching loses its long pause on Plex - the library inventory behind More Like This now refreshes in the background instead of in front of you. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.4 (versionCode 6).
### 4.8.1 (26 August 2026) - Three fixes from 4.8.0's first evening in use. Home's Continue Watching now advances to the next episode by itself - it keeps asking the server for up to two and a half minutes after playback and stops the moment the row moves, instead of only checking in the seconds after the player closed. A library deleted on the server now leaves the menu on the next request instead of surviving in a ten-minute cache. And the television help row is now simply called Help. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.4 (versionCode 6).
### 4.8.0 (26 August 2026) - Five features and one look. Protected profiles are honoured on Emby and Jellyfin - a profile with a password on the server is asked for it on the Who's watching screen, like a Plex PIN, and choosing a profile now talks to the server as that user so per-user library limits genuinely apply. A Requests tab appears when you connect Overseerr or Jellyseerr in Settings - search for anything and press Request. Around each occasion, Home dresses for the party: seasonal featured titles and a backdrop framing the billboard, switched off with the seasonal shelf's own toggle. Settings is rebuilt - on the TV a small D-pad screen with a built-in How to use CineDock guide and a QR code handing setup to a phone; in a browser everything configurable, including a Report what I watch switch. The menu bar folds extra libraries behind More instead of breaking, and on television the wordmark moves to a boot splash shown only when there is loading to cover. One colour scheme and one selection ring everywhere, and Back always undoes exactly one layer - choosing a subtitle then pressing Back no longer ends the film. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.4 (versionCode 6).
### 4.7.1 (25 August 2026) - Two things a television series was getting wrong. A finished episode now shows as watched straight away instead of only after leaving the programme and coming back, and it keeps looking for a couple of minutes because a Fire TV reports what it has played on a slow beat. A series now resumes where you were however you reached it - previously only Continue Watching remembered, and arriving from a search or a shelf restarted it from episode one; the button now says which episode it will play. Also: the brief 'what's new' notice after an update has gone - too quick to read, and its text was usually a release out of date - and a series' action icons now match a film's exactly. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.4 (versionCode 6).
### 4.7.0 (24 August 2026) - A seasonal shelf that appears only in its season and is named for it - 'Tis the Season, Fright Night, Love Is in the Air, Hop To It and Gather Round - showing the films you already own that belong to it, matched by TMDB id rather than by title. Four more kinds of shelf: Recently Watched, Top by Actor or Director, Top from a Studio, and your Playlists. Collections now appear when you search, and open the collection; the shelf picker has a search box of its own. Every smart shelf now rotates - steady through the day, different tomorrow, and different for each person in the house. Short and Sweet has been removed. Fixed: on Emby and Jellyfin, choosing a viewer's profile did not stop them playing something that profile is not allowed - it does now, and a refusal says so plainly; Plex was never affected. A series' buttons now match a film's, and episode synopses are no longer cut off. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.4 (versionCode 6).
### 4.6.2 (22 August 2026) - A maintenance release; nothing changes on screen. The container and the Windows and Mac editions are back on the same version number, where they were before 4.6.1. Behind the scenes the version now lives in a single file that the whole build reads, instead of nine separate places. The TV app is unchanged at 0.2.4 (versionCode 6).
### Desktop 4.6.1 (21 August 2026) - Windows and Mac editions only; the container stays at 4.6.0 and needs no update. The tray menu's labels are visible again - on Windows the right-click menu opened with its items working but no text on them.
### 4.6.0 (21 August 2026) - Television series pages now put programme details, seasons and image-led episode cards together on one screen. The title and actions sit beside a fixed trailer window; season buttons open episodes directly; cast, extras and an owned-library More Like This shelf remain below. The old More prompt and gap are gone, and Remove from Continue Watching has its own centred row. Film pages are unchanged. A local, no-cloud notice can now say when a newer TV app is available. Container and desktop editions are 4.6.0; the TV app remains 0.2.4 (versionCode 6). Windows and Mac also gained: a newer build now replaces an older one still in the tray rather than reopening it; a one-time note when the window is first closed saying CineDock keeps running in the tray; and a Help & user guide item in the tray menu.
### 4.5.1 (20 August 2026) - The desktop upgrade notice is now clickable and opens the right release page (desktop editions only; containers never show the notice, and nothing else changes).
### 4.5.0 (20 August 2026) - Collections: the same collection is merged across every library into one shelf, with a line saying where its titles came from (Emby, Jellyfin and Plex). A new Collections tab is the chooser: pick what appears on Home and in what order from everything your server offers; collections you made yourself arrive switched on, anything CineDock guessed at arrives off and marked New. Home is now per viewer, and Continue Watching can be moved or switched off (off, it waits at the top of the picker). Desktop editions announce a newer build beside the version number instead of only inside Settings. Fixed: a shelf change could show the old Home for up to ten minutes; switching Continue Watching back on needed a reload; row headings sat under the selection glow. Television polish: lighter selection band, menus as words rather than chips, quieter watched tick. Browsers, phones and the TV app (0.2.4) unchanged.
### 4.4.0 (19 August 2026) - The More Info screen, finished, and a line drawn under 4.3.4 and 4.3.5 (both pulled within hours after checks on a real television). Fixed: the info-screen trailer is now seen as well as heard (it played behind the page on Fire TV); Up on a film no longer marks it watched; the Spotlight artwork no longer disappears after an info screen; in Browse All the A-Z rail is no longer a dead end, Home from the menu really goes Home, and the selection is a deeper amber with the selected poster slightly enlarged; Plex "Recently Added" shows the programme rather than "Season 1"; confirm dialogs open in silence. New on the television info screen: the title's clearlogo from your server (Plex, Emby, Jellyfin), ratings with their source (IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes, TMDB), Plex-style action buttons, the director's portrait and the Dolby mark on Dolby badges. Browsers, phones and the TV app (0.2.4) unchanged.
### 4.3.5 (18 August 2026) - Completes the More Info redesign released in 4.3.4 the same day: the trailer on the info screen did not actually play on a television (it was held behind a check on a flag the Plex connection never sets - measured 0 of 25 films on Plex reporting a trailer where 20 really had one). It now plays, with sound, once, after a short pause, and stops as soon as you press Play or leave the page. The TRAILER badge follows what is really playing, and audio badges drop the technical qualifier so "5.1(side)" reads "5.1". Browsers, phones and the TV app (0.2.4) unchanged.
### 4.3.4 (18 August 2026) - The More Info screen is redesigned for televisions: the whole page now fits one screen for a film and for a long-running series alike (it ran to 1.5 and over 3 screens before), text no longer sits on artwork, and the description is larger. Media info (resolution, HDR/Dolby Vision, codec, frame rate, audio format) is shown per title and per episode, along with director, studio and country. Seasons and episodes have their own screens that open on where you are up to. Marking watched is now signposted, and the two actions that cannot be undone ask first. A trailer plays with sound in a box on the page where your server has one. Browsers, phones and the TV app (0.2.4) are unchanged.
### 4.3.3 (18 August 2026) - Zidoo support: the interface now displays correctly on Zidoo players (Z9X 8K tested) - the TV app always gets the television layout and older-engine layout gaps are filled. Pairs with the Fire TV / Shield / Zidoo app 0.2.4, which on a Zidoo plays through the box's own player. Other devices unchanged.
### 4.3.2 (17 August 2026) - Performance: first launch and every launch after an idle spell now show Home in about a second instead of 12-15 s on Plex (no more waiting on Plex to compute its hubs; Home is served from cache and refreshed in the background; pre-warmed at container start). No feature changes; Fire TV / Shield app unchanged (0.2.3).
### 4.3.1 (16 August 2026) - Bug fixes: removed an empty navy band that sat over the top menu on a TV app's first launches; Search and Requests pages no longer open under the header; in-app help points at cinedock.tv/support. Fire TV / Shield app unchanged (0.2.3).
### 4.3.0 (16 August 2026) - Browse All: every library as a full poster grid (sort, unwatched and genre filters), paged and windowed for large libraries. - A-Z rail, Genres page, and "See all" on New Releases / Recently Added / genre rows. - Library sub-menu on the second line of the top menu; inset billboard on every tab. - Fire TV fixes: rail inside overscan, "#"/"A" off-screen, grid opening low, lagging letter marker. - Works on Emby, Jellyfin and Plex. TV app unchanged (0.2.2).
### 4.2.1 (14 August 2026) - Plex artwork now delivered at display size (both dimensions sent to the transcoder); artwork cache key versioned. - Hidden Gems and Short and Sweet smart collections wired into Plex Home; Settings checkbox enabled for Plex.
### 4.2.0 (13 August 2026) - Chapter preview images via bundled ffmpeg from an optional read-only media mount (size-capped cache). - Hidden Gems and Short and Sweet smart collections across Plex, Emby and Jellyfin. - Watchlist promoted to a top-navigation destination.

Container.Description: Rediscover your library. CineDock gives Plex, Emby or Jellyfin an enhanced browsing experience on the NVIDIA Shield TV, on an Amazon Fire TV Stick, on Zidoo media players, or in a browser on your computer or tablet. CineDock does not scan, copy or change media files. Install the container, open its web page and connect your media server.
Container.DonateText: Enjoying CineDock? Support its continued development.

Config.Name: Web port
Config.Description: The port you open in your browser to use CineDock.

Config.Name: Config folder
Config.Description: Where CineDock stores its server connection and small caches.

Config.Name: TMDB API key (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. A free TMDB key adds actor biographies, filmographies and improves spotlight selection. It does not supply trailer video files. CineDock works without it.

Config.Name: Emby server address (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Full Emby address, for example http://192.168.1.20:8096. Add it with the API key to make TV setup a single connection test.

Config.Name: Emby API key (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Store the Emby API key in the container so it does not need to be entered on the television setup screen.

Config.Name: Jellyfin server address (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Full Jellyfin address, for example http://192.168.1.20:8096. Add it with the API key to make TV setup a single connection test.

Config.Name: Jellyfin API key (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Store the Jellyfin API key in the container so it does not need to be entered on the television setup screen.

Config.Name: Plex server address (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Full local Plex address, for example http://192.168.1.20:32400. Add it with the token to make Plex immediately selectable; secure account linking remains available when blank.

Config.Name: Plex token (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Store the Plex token in the container for immediate server switching, or leave blank to use secure Plex account linking.
